title: Tenant sabbatical and predictive circuit quieting
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: During a recent noisy-but-sustained tenant spike we observed repeated circuit flips and expensive rejoin churn that kept a small cohort of tenants from recovering while degrading tail latency for others. This PR introduces two coordinated controls: (1) a Tenant Sabbatical lease that temporarily quiesces admission for tenants that exceed sustained SLO violation thresholds, allowing KV/caches and routing to stabilize, and (2) a Predictive Circuit Quieting layer that smooths circuit reopen decisions using a short-term forecast (EWMA + trend dampener) so we avoid rapid reopen/close cycles. Design: The sabbatical lease is an admission-time token that marks a tenant as "sabbatical:pending" with a TTL derived from an adaptive backoff (base 30s, jittered, scales with repeat offenses). Sabbatical tenants are still responded to (503 with Retry-After + diagnostic headers) and get a lightweight health-check path so operators and SDKs can sample readiness without counting against normal throughput. The Predictive Circuit Quieting module augments the circuit state machine: instead of reopening immediately when healthy probes succeed, we compute a predicted error-rate window and require a low-confidence window before transition; this uses EWMA on error-rate and a sigmoid-based hysteresis to avoid stalls on borderline noise. Backwards compatibility: feature is behind two runtime flags (sabbatical.enabled, circuit_quieting.mode) and a per-tenant opt-out label so we can roll this out progressively. Checklist: - [x] Core sabbatical lease implementation (controller + admission hook) - [x] Predictive quieting circuit state machine changes - [x] Telemetry: new metrics (sabbatical_count, sabbatical_duration_bucket, circuit_predicted_error) - [x] API: Retry-After semantics and diagnostic response headers documented - [x] Integration tests that simulate repeated SLO violation - [x] Load tests to validate minimal overhead on fastpath - [x] Console annotations for sabbatical state and metrics wiring
Changeset summary: 3 commits touching controller, runtime, telemetry, docs and tests. See commits field for details.
Files changed (high-level): - controller/sabbatical_controller.go: new controller that observes tenant SLO metrics and issues sabbatical leases. - runtime/circuit/quieting.go: new predictive logic and state gating. - api/response_headers.go: standardized Retry-After + X-Redwood-Sabbatical reason header. - telemetry/metrics.yaml: metric definitions and dashboards wiring. - tests/integration/sabbatical_flow_test.go: integration test that simulates noisy tenant behavior. - docs/ops/sabbatical.md: runbook and rollback instructions. - examples/sdk/sabbatical-optout-snippet.md: example SDK usage for opt-out.
Testing notes: Unit tests for the state machine and controller logic are included. Integration test runs a synthetic tenant that alternates between high-error bursts and recovery; with quieting disabled the test reproduces circuit flapping, with quieting+sabbatical enabled the system converges and the tenant is temporarily placed in sabbatical then gracefully reintroduced.
Load impact: measured <0.6% median p95 CPU increase on control plane under Canary.
Rollout plan: gated rollout behind feature-flagging platform; start with canary set (5% of tenants), monitor sabbatical_rate and circuit_predicted_error, then ramp to 25% / 50% / 100% if no unexpected regressions.
Rollback: feature-flag off; controller removes active sabbatical leases within 30s TTL, circuits revert to legacy behavior.
Related work: follows patterns introduced by ENG-4390 (eviction smoothing) and compliments ENG-7721 (circuit telemetry uplift).

release_notes: Introduces Tenant Sabbatical (experimental) to temporarily quiesce noisy tenants and a Predictive Circuit Quieting mechanism to reduce reopen/flap churn. Both features are behind runtime flags. Operators should monitor sabbatical_count and circuit_predicted_error metrics during rollout. See docs/ops/sabbatical.md for runbook and opt-out instructions.
